```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)

```

```{r}
# Replace these numbers with YOUR odds ratios & CIs
charta <- data.frame(
  label = c("High income",
            "High education",
            "Urban",
            "Under 30 years",
            "Female"),
  or  = c(0.6294642,
          0.6493108,
          1.022839,
          1.045678,
          1.0167),
  
  lcl = c(0.5337256,
          0.5642022,
          0.861059,
          0.8958829,
          0.8960449),
  
  ucl = c(0.7423762,
          0.7472606,
          1.215077,
          1.216852,
          1.160595)
)

# make factor so they appear top-to-bottom like the Lancet figure
charta$label <- factor(charta$label,
                       levels = rev(charta$label))


p_a <- ggplot(charta, aes(x = or, y = label)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lcl, xmax = ucl), height = 0.2, size = 0.5, color = "#00A5B5") +
  geom_point(size = 2, shape = 23, fill = "#00A5B5", color = "#00A5B5", stroke = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5),
    limits = c(0.5, 1.5),
    labels = c("0.50","0.75","1.0","1.25","1.50"),
    expand = c(0.02, 0.02)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Odds ratio (95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Quality of public system rated highly"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    ### Text ###
    text = element_text(family = "Times"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "Times", size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1),

    ### No grid ###
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    ### LANCET AXIS STYLE ###
    # Thick bottom axis line
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5),
    # Thick left axis line
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5),

    ### Tick marks ###
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", size = 1),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(4, "pt"),   # length like the journal

    ### Title centered ###
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, family = "Times", face = "bold")
  )

p_a

ggsave("chart1.png", p_a, width = 5, height = 8, dpi = 300, units = "in")


```

# now make bar charts
```{r}
df1 <- data.frame(
  country = "USA",
  metric = c("Can get good-quality care", 
             "Can afford care when needed",
             "Can get and afford care"),
  value = c(85.20, 65.86, 62.63)
)

df1$metric <- factor(
  df1$metric,
  levels = c(
    "Can get and afford care",
    "Can afford care when needed",
    "Can get good-quality care"
  )
)

p_bar1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x = value, y = metric, fill = metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.85, color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(value, "%")), 
            hjust = -0.2, family = "Times", size = 4) +

  # Colors from Lancet figure
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Can get good-quality care" = "#E9DD8F",
    "Can afford care when needed"   = "#BFD3AD",
    "Can get and afford care" = "#AFC8DA"
  )) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0,102),
    breaks = seq(0,100,20),
    expand = c(0,0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +   # Removes vertical gaps
  labs(
    y = NULL,
    x = "Proportion of respondents feeling somewhat\nor very confident (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Times"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "Times", size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    # Axis style similar to Lancet
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(4, "pt"),

    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

p_bar1

ggsave("chart6.png", p_bar1, width = 5, height = 2, dpi = 300, units = "in")

```

```{r}
df2 <- data.frame(
  metric = "Improved in past 2 years",
  value  = 11.52
)

p_bar2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x = value, y = metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",
           width = 0.7,
           fill  = "#C9BEDF",      # soft lavender / purple
           color = "black") +      # black border like Lancet
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(value, "%"), x = value + 8),
            family = "Times",
            size   = 5) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +

  labs(
    x = "Proportion of respondents stating the health system\nhas improved in the past 2 years (%)",
    y = NULL,
    title = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Times"),
    axis.text.y  = element_blank(),      # no y-axis label
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),

    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    # Lancet-like axes
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(4, "pt"),

    legend.position = "none"
  )

p_bar2

ggsave("chart7.png", p_bar2, width = 5, height = 2, dpi = 300, units = "in")
```

```{r}
    breaks = seq(0,100,20),
    expand = c(0,0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +   # Removes vertical gaps
  labs(
    y = NULL,
    x = "Proportion of respondents stating\n\"very good\" or \"excellent\" (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Times"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "Times", size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    # Axis style similar to Lancet
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(4, "pt"),

    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

p_bar5

ggsave("chart10.png", p_bar5, width = 5, height = 2, dpi = 300, units = "in")

```

```{r}
# install.packages(c("sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata"))

library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)


# 1. Your countries
countries_to_highlight <- c(
  "Argentina","Belgium","China","Egypt","Ethiopia","Finland","Germany","Ghana",
  "Honduras","India","Italy","Japan","Kenya","Latvia","Mexico","Nepal",
  "Nigeria","Norway","Peru","Romania","Senegal","Singapore","Switzerland",
  "United States","United Kingdom", "Taiwan"
)

# 2. Define income groups for those countries
# (These are just example groupings – replace with whatever classification you want,
# e.g. World Bank income groups.)
income_df <- tibble::tibble(
  country = countries_to_highlight,
  income_group = dplyr::case_when(
    country %in% c(
      "Belgium","Finland","Germany","Italy","Japan","Latvia",
      "Norway","Singapore","Switzerland","United States","United Kingdom"
    ) ~ "HIC",
    country %in% c("Argentina","China","Taiwan","Mexico","Romania","Egypt","Ghana","Honduras","India","Kenya","Nigeria",
      "Peru","Senegal","Ethiopia","Nepal") ~ "LMIC",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
)

# 3. Get world map
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# 4. Create a join name that matches your vector (handle USA name)
world <- world %>%
  mutate(
    join_name = dplyr::case_when(
      admin == "United States of America" ~ "United States",
      TRUE ~ admin
    )
  )

# 5. Join income info onto the world map
world_income <- world %>%
  left_join(income_df, by = c("join_name" = "country"))

# 6. Plot: base world in grey, highlighted countries colored by income group
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_income, fill = "grey90", color = "grey70", size = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(
    data = subset(world_income, !is.na(income_group)),
    aes(fill = income_group),
    color = "grey20",
    size = 0.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "HIC" = "steelblue",
      "LMIC" = "#91bfdb"
    )
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = " ")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```
